rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest candidate: chunk 3 "What You'll Learn" line 13: "the gaps two sessions of the same task surface" — "two sessions of the same task" (un-packaged M4 send-off vs packaged M5 re-send) is not named until chunk 4 (line 22) within this file, but it is arc-earned from prior modules, not a new referent this file invents: grep this session confirmed `run-the-first-experiment.md` (M4) lines 20-23/51 establish the un-packaged send-off beat and `learn-from-the-test.md` (M5) lines 9/19/23/52 establish the packaged re-send beat, both read before M6 per the module sequence. Rule 1's carve-out ("the training's own named artifacts, once earned in a prior module's body ... the practice at M4+ ... don't re-earn per slide") covers exactly this shape. Chunk 4 line 24's "the lecture" (in "stay with the rescue and read the lecture afterwards") also holds: it resolves generically against whatever lecture the room is running (the link immediately after, same chunk, is the concrete case), not a specific missing antecedent.

Chunk 4 "Start here" line 22: "The un-packaged Module 4 send-off. The packaged Module 5 re-send." — names the source module by title ("Module 4", "Module 5"), not by position ("the previous module"), exactly as rule 2 asks. No other cross-file reference in the body; the six include-links (lines 28/30/32/34/36/38/45) name their targets by link text, not position.
